To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the dispersion state of tethered nanoparticles in polymer hosts is largely determined by two parameters, the ratio of particle diameter to the tethered chain size (D/d), and the ratio of host to tethered polymer molecular weights (P/N), and that tethered nanoparticles are found to form stable dispersions well beyond the P/N threshold that defines the wetting/dewing transition in polymer brushes interacting with polymer melts.
tethered nanoparticles form stable dispersive composites beyond the P/N threshold for wetting of polymer brushes on flat surfaces.

the phase stability of tethered nanoparticle composites is largely independent of tethered polymer grafting density, and that a general strategy for obtaining uniform dispersion of nanoparticles in polymers is to choose the nanoparticle diameter to be smaller than the size of the graft chain, and to use a polymer of sufficiently higher molecular weight than the graft chain.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the phase behavior of nanoparticle-polymeric composite materials and the effect of tethered polymer chains on the dispersion stability of nanoparticles.
the phase behavior of nanoparticle-polyber composites and the role of polymer tethers in controlling the dispersion state of particles and phase stability.
the development of a general framework for the dispersion state, phase behavior, and stability of polymer tether nanoparticle-polycolymer composites.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

tethered nanoparticles are more likely to form a stable dispersion in their polymer host when the particle size is smaller than the tethered chain size and when the molecular weight of the host polymer is smaller than that of the tethered polymer.
tethered nanoparticles in their polymer hosts display phase stability beyond the P/N limits that govern the stability of polymer brushes on flat surfaces.

the phase stability and dispersion state of tethered nanoparticles in a polymer matrix depends on the ratio between the size of the nanoparticle and tethered chain and on the ratio of the chain length of the polymer tether to that of the host matrix.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the phase behavior of nanoparticle composites is determined by the interfacial properties of the nanoparticle-polyloid interface.

the phase behavior of tethered nanoparticle dispersions in their host polymer is largely insensitive to grafting density and the chemistry of the host and instead is dictated by the relative sizes of the nanoparticle and tethered chain as well as the molecular weights of host and tethered polymers.
the phase behavior of tethered nanoparticle dispersions in polymer hosts is dominated by the curvature of the tethered polymers.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the dispersion state of polymer tethered nanoparticles in a polymer host can be tuned to achieve either a uniform dispersion or nanoparticle clustering by controlling the P/N ratio and the ratio of nanoparticle diameter to the tethered chain size.

the dispersion state of tethered nanoparticles in polymer hosts is determined primarily by the ratio of the tethered polymer and host chain lengths, rather than by the grafting density and chemistry of the tethered polymers.
nanoparticle-polymeric dispersions can be stabilized in the melt state by the tethered polymer layer.
